step_titles.trigger: How would you like to trigger recording?

welcome.heading: Welcome
welcome.body: A premium dictation app for Windows that runs entirely on your machine. We'll get you set up in under two minutes.

privacy.title: Everything stays on your machine
privacy.body: No cloud transcription. No cloud post-processing. No telemetry by default. Your recordings, transcripts, and preferences are stored only on this PC.

updates.title: Update checks
updates.body_suffix: if a newer version is out. This is the only outbound request the app makes by default. It sends just your current version, no usage, no telemetry, no identifiers.

options.on_description: Get a small toast when a new version is available. You always click Install yourself, nothing downloads or runs in the background.
options.off_description: Utterbar will never reach the internet. You can still check manually any time from Settings → General → "Check now".

model.title: Choose your ASR model
model.subtitle: Models run entirely on this machine. Change it later in Settings → Models.
model.multilingual_body: Pick the Whisper model below, it covers around 99 languages on the free tier.

stub.label: Skip for now
stub.body: Placeholder transcriber. You can install a real model from Settings → Models later.

download.error_generic: Download failed. Check your connection and try again.

gpu.title: Use your GPU?
gpu.body_suffix: . Running transcription on it is typically 3–10× faster than CPU. You can change this later in Settings → Advanced.

options.auto_description: Use your GPU when it helps, fall back to CPU for short clips. No surprises.
options.always_description: Fastest transcription. May briefly slow games, 3D apps, or heavy browser tabs while you dictate.
options.cpu_description: Keep the GPU free for other apps. Transcription is still fast, just a bit slower per utterance.

mic.title: Pick and test your microphone
mic.body: Choose your input device, then record a short test to confirm it's working end-to-end.
mic.no_devices: No input devices detected. Plug in a microphone or check Windows privacy settings.

baseline.title: Your typing speed baseline
baseline.body: We use this to estimate how much time you save by dictating. You can take a quick typing test, enter a number you already know, or skip for now and tune it later.

measure.timer_idle: Timer starts on your first keystroke.

skipped.body: Using the default {{wpm}} WPM. You can fine-tune this later in Settings → General → Typing baseline.
skipped.change_mind: Change my mind, take the test

sentences: The quiet morning light crept across the floor as the kettle started to whistle softly in the kitchen.
Most people only realise how much they type in a day when they stop to watch their own hands move.
A good dictation tool should feel less like a tool and more like a second, patient pair of ears listening carefully.
She picked up the notebook, turned to a fresh page, and wrote the first sentence that came into her head.
Working from home for years had taught him to value the small rituals more than the long meetings ever could.

trigger.title: How would you like to trigger recording?
trigger.subtitle: You can change this any time in Settings → Shortcuts, and bind different styles to different keys.

options.toggle_description: Press the key to start recording. Press it again to stop. Most apps work this way.
options.hold_description: Hold the key down while speaking. Release to stop. Walkie-talkie style, good for short bursts.
options.push_description: Same key does both. A quick tap toggles; holding it acts like hold-to-talk. Pick this if you want one key to handle both styles.

shortcut.title: Bind a recording shortcut
shortcut.body: You can bind a global shortcut from Settings → Shortcuts once onboarding finishes. Any key combo works in any app. Ctrl+Space is set by default.

bar.title: Where Utterbar lives
bar.body: A small bar will float near the top of your screen whenever Utterbar is running. It shows a live waveform while you dictate and lets you start, stop, or cancel with a click. You can drag it anywhere you like, and it'll remember the position.
bar.tip: Tip: grab the bar anywhere that isn't a button to drag it. Hover to see the record, stop, history, and settings controls.

ready.heading: You're ready

prompt.listening_push: Speak now, press again to stop.
prompt.listening_toggle: Speak now, press the shortcut again to stop.
prompt.success: Done, your words are in the box.
prompt.idle: Press the shortcut, speak, and your words will land in the box below.

ready.waveform_idle: Waiting for the shortcut, the waveform will come alive when you're speaking.
ready.textarea_placeholder: Your dictated text will appear here…
ready.click_start_hint: Or click Start dictating below when you're ready.
ready.warmup_body: the first dictation loads the model and takes a few seconds. Subsequent ones while the model is warm feel near-instant. Tune how long the model stays warm in Settings → Models.

vocab.title: Want Utterbar to get your name right?
vocab.body: Add it to vocabulary now and dictation will spell it correctly from the very first try. You can add more words later from Settings → Vocabulary.
vocab.save_error_generic: Could not save. Try again later.

language.title: Pick your dictation language
language.subtitle: This is the language Utterbar listens for when you dictate. The interface language is separate; this app stays in English.
language.picker_description: You can change this later in Settings → Models. Picking a non-English language here will recommend a multilingual model on the next step.

warning.english_only_body: You picked a non-English dictation language, but {{model}} is English-only. Switch to a multilingual model below.
warning.no_multilingual_body: No multilingual model is in the catalogue yet. Install Whisper from Settings → Models, then come back and pick this language again.
